title: The date
hook: Anas carries a newborn and a handful of dates across Medina

segments.voice: Yesterday: the call in the ear, the first words a child hears. After the first sound comes the first taste.

Umm Sulaym has just given birth, and her son Anas is carrying the newborn through Medina to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. She has sent some dates along with him. Anas tells the story in Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase. The Prophet takes the baby and asks: is there anything with him? Yes, some dates. He takes one, chews it until it's soft, and puts a little of it into the baby's mouth. Today's word is that small act: tahnik.
screen: `ANAS CARRIES A NEWBORN.` → `IS THERE ANYTHING WITH HIM?` → `A SOFTENED DATE FOR THE BABY.`

segments.voice: In Bukhari, the Prophet then named the baby 'Abdullah. Sahih Muslim keeps a fuller telling, in paraphrase: the baby moved his tongue and licked at the date, and the Prophet said, see the Ansar's love of dates. The Ansar were the people of Medina, and dates were their harvest. A joke, a taste and a name, all in one visit. And it happens again. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari tells, in Bukhari, in paraphrase: a son was born to me, and I took him to the Prophet. He named him Ibrahim, did tahnik for him with a date, prayed for blessing for him, and gave him back to me. So it wasn't a single moment in one family; the Prophet did it more than once, when newborns were brought to him. What is it? A date is softened, by chewing or by mashing, and a little is touched to the inside of the baby's mouth, at the palate. In Abu Musa's report it comes with a du'a for blessing. Some Muslim families still keep the custom, and some ask a respected, pious person to do it. Why a date? The texts don't explain it, and it's honest to say so. They only show it: in the moment of welcome, the Prophet reached for something sweet. Before the baby could know a single word, he gave it a taste, and a prayer.
screen: `SEE HOW THE ANSAR LOVE DATES.` · `ABU MUSA: IBRAHIM, A DATE, A DU'A.` · `A SOFTENED DATE TO THE PALATE.` · `THE TEXTS SHOW IT; THEY DON'T EXPLAIN.`

segments.voice: If you have a date or anything sweet nearby, hold it, or picture one, and look at it before you take one slow bite. Let it sit on your tongue the way it would for someone tasting sweetness for the first time. If you pray, you can say bismillah before and alhamdulillah after; if not, simply notice the sweetness, and who might have made it reach you.
Tahnik. Touching a softened date to a newborn's palate, with a prayer for blessing, as the Prophet did for babies brought to him. Today's word.
Your line: sweetness first. A taste and a prayer, before any word. Back tomorrow, same hill.

howItsDone: Muslim families who keep the custom perform tahnik soon after birth: a softened date is touched to the inside of the baby's mouth, sometimes by a respected or pious person, with a du'a for blessing.

notes: Hadith numbers to confirm: Bukhari 5467, 5470. In 5470 the baby is the son of Abu Talhah and Umm Sulaym; Anas is Umm Sulaym's son. Confirm details (Umm Sulaym sending the baby; the Prophet's remark about the Ansar).
